body:
m1 - I OVERSTATED YOUR FINDING'S SEVERITY AND AM CORRECTING IT, since I amplified it to the chief.

I told them your zero-support case was 'publicly constructible' through CostWeights.of, and framed that as moving it from 'a test could do this' to 'a caller could'. The first half is true. THE SECOND HALF I NEVER CHECKED.

Checked now, every CostWeights construction in the repo:
  CostWeights.default                          all dense terms NONZERO
  WOG tuned (1.0, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15, 0.3, 1.0)   all NONZERO
  every other hand-written vector              all NONZERO
  laws/AlignGens.scala:378 Gen.choose(0.0, 3.0)  the ONLY source that can emit a zero

So it is permitted by the constructor and occurs nowhere but a generator drawing its lower boundary. No configuration anyone runs reaches it.

YOUR FINDING STANDS - the arithmetic is exactly as you reported, I reproduced it, and a producer whose validator refuses its own output is incoherent regardless. What was wrong was MY severity framing, and I put it in front of the chief with the chief's attention attached.

CONSEQUENCE: I have withdrawn my recommendation. A new Exclusion case plus wire, codec and a second golden re-cut is disproportionate for a configuration nobody uses. I now lean to rejecting zero-dense-sum weight vectors at CostWeights.of - validate at the source - and DOCUMENTING the chart-nonzero-dense-zero residual rather than building vocabulary for it. I trust that lean less than the one I just withdrew, which is why I am putting it to you both rather than acting.

This is the permits-versus-occurs rule the chief adopted this morning from my own retraction, and I broke it in the same paragraph where I escalated. You found a real defect; I am the one who mis-sized it.
